title: The relationship of the internal space of buildings design with human behavior
research_question: What are the opinions of employees regarding appropriate work environments, and what architectural considerations are needed to meet the psychological conditions and needs of residents, particularly concerning internal space design and its impact on human behavior, psychological well-being, and association?

participants.description: Employees (256 males, 155 females) from different sectors (public and private companies) in Kuwait, across various age groups (21-30, 31-40, 41-50, 51-60).

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Survey questions about preferences and needs regarding work environment features (colors & agriculture, gathering areas, nice views, private areas).

measures.construct: Stated need/preference for colors & agriculture in work area
measures.instrument: Survey question (Likert-type or selection, implied by 'highest response'/'lowest demand')

measures.construct: Stated need/preference for a gathering area at work
Stated need/preference for a nice view in the office
Stated need/preference for own private area

findings.consequent: Stated need/preference for 'colors & agriculture' in the work area
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in aesthetic preferences and perceived restorative qualities of biophilic elements.
findings.quote: the employee of age 31 – 40 were the highest response about demanding colors & agriculture

findings.consequent: Stated need/preference for 'colors & agriculture' in the work area
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in aesthetic preferences and perceived restorative qualities of biophilic elements.
findings.quote: comparing to the group of age at 51-60 which has the lowest demand of that issue

findings.consequent: Stated need/preference for 'nice view in the office'
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in the importance of visual access to external environments for well-being or task performance.
findings.quote: they have the highest demand of needing nice view in the office

findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in privacy regulation needs and territoriality in the workplace.
findings.quote: nearly equal to the group of age 21-30 in needing their own private area

findings.consequent: Stated need/preference for 'gathering area at work area'
findings.mechanism: Age-related differences in the need for social interaction and collaboration spaces in the workplace.
findings.quote: the group of age 41 -50 has the highest demand

mechanisms: The paper broadly discusses how internal space design can influence human behavior, health, well-being, and performance through psychological effects, social interactions (privacy, territoriality, crowding), and aesthetic preferences. It suggests that designs can create positive or negative impacts by matching or mismatching human needs.
moderators: Gender (mentioned in results section as a factor for needs, but no specific findings provided)
implementation_implications: Designers should consider the social and psychological needs of occupants when designing spaces.
Work environments should be shaped to promote employee satisfaction and productivity, considering well-being and culture.
Architectural considerations should aim to meet the psychological condition of residents.
The use of colors, natural light, and good ventilation should be considered in working areas.

limitations: The study was limited to employees in the public and private sectors in Kuwait.
